tools.name: list_calls
tools.description: List Gong calls in a date window, with title, timing, direction and the primary user on each call

from_date_time.description: Start of the window, ISO-8601 with offset (e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z). Gong filters on the call start time.

to_date_time.description: End of the window, ISO-8601 with offset (e.g. 2026-09-08T00:00:00Z)

workspace_id.description: Optional Gong workspace ID to restrict the results to

cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor from a previous call's cursor value

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List Gong users (seats) with name, email, title, manager and active state

cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor from a previous call's cursor value

tools.name: get_call
tools.description: Get one Gong call by ID (metadata only: title, timing, direction, primary user)

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED, and it matches the vault entry byte for byte: Basic base64(access_key:access_key_secret). services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js key 'gong' (line 5784) collects access_key and access_key_secret and its testHeaders builds `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${creds.access_key}:${creds.access_key_secret}`).toString('base64')}` against testEndpoint https://api.gong.io/v2/users, which is exactly what auth {type: basic, userField access_key, passField access_key_secret} plus test GET /v2/users sends. No new vault field was needed and none was invented.

SHAPE-PROOF RESULT (real run, 2026-09-12, 1 iteration): verbatim overall line 'gong  SHAPE_PROVEN  proven=4 authwall=0 ambiguous=0 failed=0 inconclusive=0 skipped=0'. READ THAT CLASS DOWN TO AUTH_WALL: the harness overstated it here and the paths are NOT proven by this run. The control probe at the bogus path https://api.gong.io/quox-shapeproof-control-cb37790a answered 401 with the SAME message as every real path, verbatim {"requestId" : "3shzh6otjw21wyidufm", "errors" : [ "Validate credentials failed. Please check your credentials and try again." ]}, so Gong's auth wall sits in front of its routing. The classifier could not see that: its structuredErrorCode() returns null for a Gong body because Gong's `errors` is an array of plain strings rather than objects carrying code or message, so controlIdentical() fell back to comparing body hashes, and those differ only because Gong stamps a unique per-response requestId. Verified directly: structuredErrorCode() returns null for both the real body and the control body. WHAT IS ACTUALLY PROVEN: DNS, TLS, the host api.gong.io, base_url, and that the Basic credential is parsed and rejected (401 plus a WWW-Authenticate header on every call). WHAT IS NOT: the four paths, which rest on documentary provenance only, and any 2xx, because no Gong credential was held.

RESPONSE PICKS ARE DOCUMENTARY, NOT OBSERVED. list_calls and list_users are shaped for Gong's paged envelope ({records: {totalRecords, currentPageSize, cursor}} plus a calls[] or users[] array) and get_call for the single-object envelope {requestId, call: {...}}. None of those bodies has been seen on this connector, so any pick may be over- or under-selective; the cursor field is what a caller feeds back to page.

CALL DATE WINDOW: from_date_time and to_date_time render to Gong's fromDateTime and toDateTime and must be ISO-8601 with an offset (2026-09-01T00:00:00Z). Behaviour when they are omitted is Gong's own default and is NOT verified here, and Gong rejects a malformed or over-long window with a 400 that is a caller error, not a wiring fault.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: all three tools are GETs and none is marked write:true. The richer conversation data (call parties, transcripts, interaction stats) lives behind POST /v2/calls/extensive and POST /v2/calls/transcript, which take a JSON filter body; they are read-only in intent but POST-shaped, and they are deliberately not modelled in this draft. Gong's CRM and data-import write endpoints are likewise unmodelled.

PROVIDER RATE LIMITS ARE TIGHTER THAN THE SPEC BLOCK IMPLIES. rateLimit is the wave-standard {windowMs 60000, max 30}; Gong documents its own per-key ceiling of 3 calls per second plus a daily API call cap, so a burst issued back to back can earn a 429 from Gong even while the spec's own window has budget left. A 429 here is the provider talking, not a defect in this spec.
